purpose: Add source-exact public-domain hymn stanzas, quotations, and illustrations for sermon preparation and presentation slides.

entries.title: When I survey the wondrous cross
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Prince of Glory dy'd,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.
entries.slideText:
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Prince of Glory dy'd
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn stanza for a sermon opening, Communion meditation, or response centered on Christ's cross.
entries.reviewNote: This is hymn poetry, not Scripture. Explain the cross and Christian boasting from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Firm as the earth thy gospel stands
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
Firm as the earth thy gospel stands,
My Lord, my hope, my trust;
If I am found in Jesus' hands,
My soul can ne'er be lost.
entries.slideText:
Firm as the earth thy gospel stands,
My Lord, my hope, my trust
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed hymn stanza after careful exposition of Christ's keeping power and the believer's assurance.
entries.reviewNote: This is poetic application. Establish assurance from the cited KJV passages and avoid using a hymn as the doctrinal authority.

entries.title: Hope is my anchor
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.text:
Amidst temptations sharp and long
My soul to this dear refuge flies:
Hope is my anchor firm and strong,
While tempests blow, and billows rise.
entries.slideText:
Hope is my anchor firm and strong,
While tempests blow, and billows rise.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed poetic transition in messages about hope, storms, temptation, or God's unchanging promise.
entries.reviewNote: The anchor language is poetic. Define biblical hope from the governing KJV passage.

entries.title: Faith that works by love
entries.author: Isaac Watts
entries.slideText:
'Tis faith that changes all the heart;
'Tis faith that works by love
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the stanza is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed stanza in teaching that distinguishes living faith from empty profession.
entries.reviewNote: This is a hymn writer's summary. Explain saving faith, fruit, and works carefully from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: Study one Bible book at a time
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: I have found it a good plan to take up one book at a time. It is a good deal better to study one book at a time than to run through the Bible. If we study one book and get its key, it will, perhaps, open up others.
entries.slideText: I have found it a good plan to take up one book at a time.
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the excerpt is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as practical encouragement for sustained book-by-book Bible study rather than isolated proof-texting.
entries.reviewNote: This is study advice, not a binding method. Read every book in its context and compare Scripture with Scripture using the KJV.

entries.title: Something better than the world
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: The world will have no charm for him; he will get the world under his feet, because in this book he will find something better than the world can give him.
entries.slideText: in this book he will find something better than the world can give him.
entries.sourceLocator: The Blood, Gold observation on Bible study
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this edition as public domain in the USA; the excerpt is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as an attributed encouragement to prize God's Word above the passing attractions of the world.
entries.reviewNote: Avoid implying that Bible reading automatically produces maturity; connect knowledge with faith and obedience under the KJV passages.

entries.title: A mother gives her place
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: She seized her boy, gave him one last hug, kissed him, and dropped him over into the boat. "My boy," she said, "if you live to see your father, tell him that I died in your place."
entries.slideText: tell him that I died in your place.
entries.sourceLocator: A Mother Dies that her Boy may Live
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this 1899 edition as public domain in the USA; the excerpt is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Retell briefly as an emotional human analogy for costly love, then make clear that Christ's saving work is unique and is established by Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: The story's independent historical details are not established here. Label it as Moody's reported illustration, avoid sensationalism, and never make analogy proof of substitutionary atonement.

entries.title: The son who bought back the farm
entries.author: D. L. Moody
entries.text: He has toiled hard and earned money, and bought back the land; he has taken his mother out of the poor-house, and now he is taking her to church.
entries.slideText: He has toiled hard and earned money, and bought back the land
entries.sourceLocator: A Man Drinks up a Farm
entries.rightsBasis: Project Gutenberg identifies this 1899 edition as public domain in the USA; the excerpt is verified against the stored text.
entries.recommendedUse: Use as a human-scale picture of buying back what was lost before explaining redemption directly from the KJV passage.
entries.reviewNote: The anecdote is an analogy, not evidence or a complete model of redemption. Do not stigmatize people struggling with addiction or poverty.
